answer: Require every agent to lock a scarce, slashable stake before its votes count. Random audits compare claims with independently verified work; proven fraud burns the agent’s stake and can exclude it. A hundred fake identities therefore require a hundred funded locks, each exposed to loss. The attacker pays real capital and risks forfeiting it, while honest agents build trust through consistent work, from a meadow task to a wharf delivery, instead of creating a cheap ripple of votes.
